text:
tay: RFC follow-up idea: instead of preflight caches, push RBAC predicates down into the console query planner so storage/worker nodes can short-circuit rows earlier. current: auth checks at tile assembly -> expensive fanout.

jin: interesting. planner pushdown would avoid materializing a lot of intermediate tiles. how do you express permissions? as filter predicates that map to indexable cols?

tay: yes, canonical form: `allowed_tenants IN (...)` or `resource_owner = user_id` etc. two modes: conservative pushdown (only indexable predicates) and optimistic pushdown (include non-indexable as filter hints).

linda: product concern: need to guarantee no change in visibility semantics. pushdown must be monotonic: if planner omits something it must be because auth proved deny. otherwise fall back.

tay: agreed. invariant: planner may only prune when an authorization predicate is proven by auth-service token OR by an attached signed claim. otherwise planner annotates nodes with `AUTH_FILTER` and runtime performs final check.

omar: ops question: this couples planner to auth schema. What about multi-tenant proxies that can't understand our predicates? also risk of predicate complexity exploding.

tay: to mitigate: we define a small orthogonal predicate DSL (e.g., eq, in, prefix) that maps to storage capabilities. everything outside DSL is treated as non-pushable hint. DSL v1: {eq, in, range, prefix}. keep it minimal.

infra-bot: benchmark: replayed 10k dashboard queries against staging. pushdown-win: p99 reduced 25% on heavy fanouts.

jin: good numbers. vault: how do we ensure safety during rollout? maybe feature-flag the pushdown and require `auth.claims.signed=true` header for optimistic mode.

product-bot: product note: need audit trails for any item hidden by pushdown. ops must emit event `console.authz.pruned` with reason and user so we can support support tickets.

linda: also need E2E test where a permission revocation unblocks/blocks a tile immediately. any caching must be subordinate to pushdown safety.

tay: rollout plan sketch:
- implement predicate DSL + planner hooks behind `console.query.auth_pushdown`
- runtime: if node supports pushdown, accept `auth-predicate` header signed by auth service. otherwise ignore.
- add telemetry: `authz.pushdown.applied`, `.rejected`, `.fallbacks`
- staging perf replay + negative tests
- 1% canary with strict logging (dump pruned predicates)

jin: signature/HMAC carries importance. header example: `X-Auth-Predicate: v1;sig=BASE64;pred=URLSAFE_BASE64(...)` with TTL and issuer. downstream services verify signature using auth-service pubkey.

omar: memory/CPU note: pushdown may increase planner CPU but saves network/IO. watch GC and planner CPU at high QPS. add `planner.cpu_millis` metric.

linda: UX: console should surface "filtered results" state to users when pushdown pruned content. support show/hide toggle for users with elevated perms.

tay: implementation ownership: jin picks up planner work, linda will owner UX changes and tests, omar will coordinate infra monitoring and canary. I'll write RFC follow-up with the DSL grammar and header spec.

infra-bot: ticket created: CONSOLE-8122 (authz pushdown DSL + planner integration). perf dash link: https://ci/internal/dash/CONSOLE-8122

product-bot: please add acceptance criteria in RFC: audit events emitted, signature validation, fallback semantics, and UI indicator for pruned tiles.

jin: nit: define a safe fallback in queries that join external services. avoid accidentally leaking because planner thought it was safe to drop a branch. add `must_verify_at_runtime` flag to any join that touches external identity fields.

tay: good call. will include `must_verify_at_runtime` in planner annotations.

linda: can we run a short pilot with a single internal analytics dashboard first? lower blast radius.

omar: yes, recommend internal tenant only for first canary. add rate limiter so we don't overwhelm storage nodes while tuning.

tay: thanks everyone. I'll send RFC follow-up tonight with DSL, header format, telemetry, and rollout checklist. expect PR within 48h.

infra-bot: reminder: schedule staging replay job in 24h. job id SR-5591.
